To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

high quality people cent red and integrated care is a complex and dynamic construct for which there are currently no universally agreed conceptual frameworks available and that the available evidence is predominantly focused on advanced economies.
High quality people centered integrated care is a concept for which there is currently no agreed definition available.
High quality people centered and integrated care is a complex concept that is not yet fully understood and that requires further research.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is the state of the art of policies, programmes, and interventions on highquality people centred integrated health services? Which policies, programmes, or interventions are of relevance to the WHO strategy on People centred and Intergrated Health Services? What is the evidence on the impact of the policies, programmes, interventions? Which gaps in the evidence base are identified?
the following question: How can we improve people centred and high quality integrated care?

the development of an evidence based framework that can guide health policy makers and health care professionals in their efforts to develop and implement high quality people cent red integrated care.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is an abundance of policies, programmes, and interventions on people centred integrated health services.
the evidence on high quality people centre and integrated care is scarce, and the evidence that is available is of low quality.
there is no single policy or programme that can be identified that is the best approach for all countries, regions or localities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
high quality people cented and integrated care is a complex concept that needs to be further developed and refined, and for which there is limited empirical evidence available.
the evidence on policies, programmes or interventions that are relevant in relation to the construct of high quality people centered integrated care is limited.

there are a lot of initiatives and programmes that aim to integrate health services and to improve people centred care, but there is a lack of a coherent strategy to achieve high quality integrated care.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is an increasing interest in people centred integrated health care and that there are a number of promising policies, strategies, and interventions that have been developed to address this.

the evidence base on high quality people centre integrated care is very limited and that there is an urgent need to develop a comprehensive conceptual framework for high quality people cent red and integrated care conducive to Universal Health Coverage (UHC).
the WHO should develop a comprehensive framework that includes all elements that are of relevance to high quality people centered and integrated care conducive to the UHC.
